svg.data-what: the heart cut in a frontal plane, seen from the front: its right side, with oxygen-poor blood in blue, is on the left of the picture

g.data-what: the pulmonary trunk and its two branches, carrying oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs
the aorta, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle to the whole body, arching over to descend behind the heart

path.data-what: the inferior vena cava, bringing oxygen-poor blood back from the lower body
the pulmonary veins, bringing oxygen-rich blood back from the lungs to the left atrium
the heart muscle (myocardium), thin around the right ventricle, thick around the left
the superior vena cava, bringing oxygen-poor blood back from the head and arms
the interventricular septum, the thick wall of muscle between the two ventricles
the right atrium, receiving oxygen-poor blood from the body through the venae cavae
the right ventricle, pumping oxygen-poor blood up into the pulmonary artery, toward the lungs
the left atrium, receiving oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins
the left ventricle, the strongest chamber, pumping oxygen-rich blood into the aorta, to the whole body

g.data-what: the tricuspid valve, between the right atrium and the right ventricle: three flaps that stop blood flowing back
the mitral valve, between the left atrium and the left ventricle: two flaps
the pulmonary valve, at the exit of the right ventricle: three pocket-like cusps
the aortic valve, at the exit of the left ventricle: three pocket-like cusps
